meta.title: Propose your token as Frankencoin collateral
meta.description: How token issuers list a new collateral on Frankencoin: proposal fee, initialization period, FCS veto and what makes a good collateral.

hero.title: Let your holders borrow francs against your token.
hero.subtitle: Frankencoin is permissionless: anyone can propose a new collateral type. If FCS holders do not veto it during the initialization period, it goes live.

items.title: Discuss first
items.body: Share your token and the terms you have in mind with the community. Proposals that were discussed are far more likely to pass.

items.title: Propose
items.body: Open the position with your terms: liquidation price, limit, interest, maturity and reserve. A 1'000 ZCHF fee goes to the reserve.

items.title: Initialization
items.body: For at least five days, FCS holders can veto. If no one does, the collateral is live and others can borrow against it.

items.title: Liquid market
items.description: Auctions must be able to sell the token quickly if a position is challenged.

items.title: Conservative terms
items.description: A liquidation price well below the market price gives the system room in a crash.

items.title: Transparent issuer
items.description: Clear legal structure and public information about the asset behind the token.

items.title: Sensible limit
items.description: Start small. The limit can be raised later with a new proposal.

faq.a: Anyone with 1'000 ZCHF for the fee and enough of the token for the initial position.
No. Frankencoin does not use price oracles. The liquidation price is set in the proposal and defended by challenges and auctions.
The proposal is denied and the fee stays in the reserve. You can try again with different terms.
